parsedVerdict.reasoning: This file fails the rule. Appointment.ts sits in the business (domain) layer, and most of it fits that role: it defines the appointment status type, and endsAt(), overlaps() and cancel() hold real scheduling rules, including the "cancel up to two hours before start" rule. The problem is that the class is also marked up as a TypeORM table mapping: @Entity() is on the class and @Column() is on the `id` field. Saying how an object is stored in a database is a persistence job, which belongs to the infrastructure layer (src/persistence/**), not to a domain entity. I'm not judging which files import which, since a separate tool checks that. The issue is that the domain class itself declares its own storage mapping.
